Get the param objects of a pipeline

Source: R/pipeline.R
pub_get_params.Rd

Returns the params stored in a pipeline or view as a named list, e.g. to build a parameter UI. If a name occurs in several steps, the first occurrence that is a param counts. So, unlike pipeflow::pip_get_params(), a plain default of an earlier step does not hide the param of a later step (see Examples).

Usage

pub_get_params(x, ..., order = c("config", "pipeline"))

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pipeline or view.

...

Optional named arguments that filter the params by their attributes, e.g. source = "user" keeps the params with exactly that source. Several filters are combined with "and", that is, a param is kept only if it matches all of them, e.g. source = "user", area = "analysis" keeps the user params of the analysis area. NULL keeps the params without the attribute (source = NULL: params with no source). No filter keeps all params. See also "Parameter filters" in the Examples.

order

"pipeline": order of first use in the pipeline. "config": order of the config (attribute order); params without it follow in pipeline order.

Value

Named list of param objects; names that the pipeline holds only as plain values are left out.

Details

Order

The params are listed in the order in which the pipeline first uses their names, also as plain defaults. With order = "config" they follow the order of their config instead (see param_config()).

Setting params

Set values with pipeflow::pip_set_params(). pubflow extends it as follows:

  • A plain value is merged into the param stored in each step (label, choices and validity are kept) and checked.

  • A param object replaces the stored one (and is checked too).

  • Steps that store a plain value get the plain value.

  • If any value is invalid or can't be merged (e.g. a group value without the names of the children), nothing is set and one error (pipeflow_set_params_error) lists all problems in its field errors, a data.frame with columns step, name and message.

  • validate = FALSE skips the validity check.

Some hints:

  • Apply a config, e.g. at the end of a pipeline constructor, with pip_set_params(x, config, unknown = "error"). The last argument catches names the pipeline does not know.

  • Inside a step, pip_set_params(.self, ...) can be used to set derived params for later steps.

  • On a view, you can set the params of the view's steps. The values still go to every step of the pipeline that has them, unless scope = "view" is used, which updates only the view's steps. Note that in the latter case, steps outside the view keep their old values, so the same param may hold different values in different steps.

  • After combining pipelines with rbind(), steps also may hold different objects of the same name (pipeflow warns if their values differ). To end up with one definition per name, apply the merged configs, in which the first (more specific) definition wins: param_config(..., .duplicates = "first").

Defaults of step functions

Step functions (added with pipeflow::pip_add()) are always defined with plain defaults, e.g. \(x = 1) and not \(x = numeric_param(1)). The param config is then applied on top, so the steps hold the param objects. This means that for a choice, the plain default is a factor that must carry the choice levels, e.g. factor("none", levels = c("none", "log")).

  • pipeflow warns (pipeflow_param_conflict) if you add or replace a step with a default that clashes with the value in existing steps, e.g. pip_add(p, "new_step", \(x = 2) ...) while other steps have x = 1.

  • pipeflow::pip_replace() takes the params from the new function's arguments. To keep the param objects and their current values, use keep_params = TRUE.

Locked params

Param UIs show params with a locked = TRUE attribute (e.g. fixed by a config) as disabled inputs. pub_pipeline_params_server() also disables the params that belong to locked steps (see pipeflow::pip_lock()), as a change could not reach them. See also "Locked params" in pub_params_ui().

See also

pipeflow::pip_set_params(), param_config(), pub_params_table(), pub_pipeline_params_server()

Examples

p <- pipeflow::pip_new("demo") |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("prep", \(yUnit = "") yUnit) |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("plot", \(ylab = "y", yUnit = "") paste(ylab, yUnit))
cfg <- param_config(
    ylab = param("Response", label = "y-axis label", source = "user"),
    yUnit = param("%", label = "Unit", source = "user")
)
# Set in step 'plot' only, so the plain default of step 'prep' comes first
pipeflow::pip_set_params(pipeflow::pip_view(p, step = "plot"), cfg, scope = "view")

pipeflow::pip_get_params(p)$yUnit  # plain default of step 'prep'
#> [1] ""
pub_get_params(p)$yUnit            # param object of step 'plot'
#> param<character>: %
#>   label: Unit
#>   source: user
#>   order: 2
#>   validity: <function>


# Parameter filters: keep the params whose attributes match
p <- pipeflow::pip_new("demo") |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("fit", \(level = 0.95, xVar = "x", nMin = 3) level)
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, param_config(
    level = numeric_param(0.95, label = "Level", source = "user",
                          area = "analysis"),
    xVar = param("x", label = "Predictor", source = "data", area = "analysis"),
    nMin = numeric_param(3, label = "Minimum n", source = "internal")
))
names(pub_get_params(p, source = "user"))
#> [1] "level"
names(pub_get_params(p, area = "analysis"))
#> [1] "level" "xVar" 
names(pub_get_params(p, source = "data", area = "analysis"))  # all must match
#> [1] "xVar"
names(pub_get_params(p, area = NULL))  # params without an area
#> [1] "nMin"


# Setting merges plain values into the params and validates them
p <- pipeflow::pip_new("demo") |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("fit", \(alpha = 0.05,
                               method = factor("a", c("a", "b"))) {
        paste(alpha, method)
    })
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, param_config(
    alpha = numeric_param(0.05, label = "Alpha", min = 0, max = 1),
    method = choice_param("a", choices = c("a", "b"), label = "Method")
), unknown = "error")
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, list(alpha = 0.1, method = "b"))
pub_get_params(p)$method
#> param<factor>: <factor[1]: b>
#>   levels: a, b
#>   label: Method
#>   order: 2
#>   validity: <function>

err <- tryCatch(
    pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, list(alpha = 2, method = "c")),
    pipeflow_set_params_error = identity
)
err$errors
#>   step   name                                     message
#> 1  fit  alpha value must be less than or equal to max (1)
#> 2  fit method                  value must be one of: a, b


# A pipeline with the same param in two steps, used in the next examples
make_pipeline <- function() {
    pipeflow::pip_new("demo") |>
        pipeflow::pip_add("fit", \(alpha = 0.05, level = 0.95) alpha) |>
        pipeflow::pip_add("plot", \(alpha = 0.05) alpha) |>
        pipeflow::pip_set_params(
            param_config(
                alpha = numeric_param(0.05, label = "Alpha", min = 0, max = 1),
                level = numeric_param(0.95, label = "Level", locked = TRUE)
            ),
            unknown = "error"
        )
}
alpha_values <- function(p) {
    vapply(pipeflow::pip_get_params(p, simplify = FALSE)$alpha, as.numeric, 1)
}


# A view: values go to every step that has the param, unless scope = "view"
p <- make_pipeline()
plot_view <- pipeflow::pip_view(p, step = "plot")
pipeflow::pip_set_params(plot_view, list(alpha = 0.1))
alpha_values(p)
#>  fit plot 
#>  0.1  0.1 
pipeflow::pip_set_params(plot_view, list(alpha = 0.2), scope = "view")
alpha_values(p)
#>  fit plot 
#>  0.1  0.2 


# Replacing a step: keep_params = TRUE keeps the param objects and their values
p <- make_pipeline()
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, list(alpha = 0.2))
new_plot <- \(alpha = 0.05) alpha * 2
kept <- pipeflow::pip_replace(p, "plot", new_plot, keep_params = TRUE)
alpha_values(kept)
#>  fit plot 
#>  0.2  0.2 

p <- make_pipeline()
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, list(alpha = 0.2))
replaced <- suppressWarnings(pipeflow::pip_replace(p, "plot", new_plot))
alpha_values(replaced)  # the plain default of the new function
#>  fit plot 
#> 0.20 0.05 


# Locked params and steps: the Shiny module shows both as disabled inputs
p <- make_pipeline()
names(pub_get_params(p, locked = TRUE))
#> [1] "level"

# pip_set_params() skips locked steps, so the values would drift apart
pipeflow::pip_lock(pipeflow::pip_view(p, step = "fit"))
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, list(alpha = 0.3))
alpha_values(p)
#>  fit plot 
#> 0.05 0.30
